long_biography.plain_text:
Anthony O. R. Baldridge’s financial life joined Wall Street work with a family stake in American steel. A Cornell graduate, he led Baldridge and Son in New York until retiring from the brokerage in 1929. After his father died, 51,633 National Steel shares were divided equally between Baldridge and his brother, architect J. Lakin Baldridge.

Baldridge died in 1957 at 58, leaving most of his estate in trust for his wife. His will directed nearly all of the remaining trust to Cornell after her death. The university later announced a $4.69 million bequest and listed the stockbroker among posthumous benefactors whose gifts supported its work.
